<reason>B establishes a distinct preventive obligation that prosecuting attackers does not supply, supported by platforms’ control over campaign distribution. A meaningfully challenges whether compliance protections eliminate incentives for over-removal, but B acknowledges residual risk and narrows its duty to actionable warnings and proportionate precautions. A never adequately weighs that remaining risk against preventable harm in clear cases. Its repeated claim that existing criminal prohibitions make platform duties duplicative leaves B’s central justification intact.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s distinction between an attacker’s misconduct and a platform’s avoidable omission defeats A’s “same facts, deeper pocket” argument. A’s strongest response—that credibility and proportionality remain litigable despite a safe harbor—limits B’s assurances, but does not establish that bounded liability inevitably requires suppressing lawful coordination.</best_rebuttal>
